Q75026: Industrial city in Liaoning on the Hun River, east of Shenyang.
Has one of the largest open-pit coal mines in Asia (West Open Pit Mine).
The last emperor Puyi was held in the Fushun War Criminals Management Centre for 'reeducation'.
Near Hetu Ala, the first capital of the Manchu leader Nurhaci.
Q994: Capital of Georgia, on the Kura River in the Caucasus.
Founded in the 5th century by King Vakhtang I; the name comes from 'warm' for its sulphur hot springs.
Its old town has sulphur bathhouses, the Narikala fortress and colourful balconied houses.
Seat of the Russian Caucasus Viceroyalty from 1801 to 1917.
Q650908: Town in southwestern Central Java, capital of Banyumas Regency.
Sits at the foot of Mount Slamet, Java's second-highest volcano.
Known for the Banyumasan dialect and mendoan (half-fried tempeh).
Q125434: Port city in the Eastern Cape, known as Port Elizabeth until 2021.
Founded in 1820 for British settlers; named after the governor's late wife Elizabeth.
A centre of South Africa's car industry (Volkswagen, Isuzu).
Called the 'Friendly City' and the 'Windy City'; Addo Elephant National Park is nearby.
Q993859: The second-largest city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, in the Peshawar Valley.
The Ashoka rock edicts at Shahbaz Garhi (3rd century BC) are among the earliest writing in South Asia.
The Takht-i-Bahi Buddhist monastery nearby is a World Heritage Site.
Home of the Guides regiment of the British Indian Army.
Q900: Capital of Tatarstan, on the Volga; a meeting point of Russian and Tatar cultures.
Capital of the Kazan Khanate until Ivan the Terrible conquered it in 1552.
Its Kremlin, with the Qolşärif Mosque and an Orthodox cathedral side by side, is a World Heritage Site.
Tolstoy and Lenin studied at its university; calls itself Russia's 'third capital'.
Q134635: Capital of Saitama Prefecture, north of Tokyo; formed in 2001 by merging Urawa, Ōmiya and other towns.
Ōmiya is a major railway hub with the Railway Museum.
Known for bonsai (Ōmiya Bonsai Village) and football (Urawa Red Diamonds).
The Saitama Super Arena is one of Japan's largest event halls.
Q14499: Capital of East Kalimantan, the most populous city on Borneo.
Lies on the Mahakam River; grew with timber, coal and oil.
Near the site of Nusantara, Indonesia's planned new capital.
Q2875992: City in Dhaka Division, Bangladesh, in the haor wetlands region.
The Sholakia Eidgah hosts one of the largest Eid prayer gatherings in South Asia.
Was a jute, rice and fish trading town on the rivers.
Q132997: Capital of Santa Catarina, mostly on Santa Catarina Island.
Has about 60 beaches and is a surfing and tourism hotspot.
Settled by colonists from the Azores in the 18th century.
Has one of the highest quality-of-life scores among Brazilian cities and a growing tech scene.
Q171771: Capital of Odisha, called the 'Temple City of India' for its hundreds of old Hindu temples.
The Lingaraj Temple (11th century) is the largest temple of the city.
With Puri and Konark it forms Odisha's 'Golden Triangle'; the Udayagiri and Khandagiri Jain caves are nearby.
Planned as a new capital in 1948 by German architect Otto Königsberger; co-hosted the 2018 Hockey World Cup.
Q3274: Capital of Nicaragua, on the shore of Lake Managua.
Chosen as capital in 1852 as a compromise between rival cities León and Granada.
Destroyed by earthquakes in 1931 and 1972; the old cathedral still stands as a ruin.
Q199605: The largest city of northeast India, on the Brahmaputra River in Assam.
Called the 'Gateway to Northeast India'; includes Dispur, the state capital.
The Kamakhya Temple on Nilachal Hill is an important Hindu goddess shrine.
Ancient Pragjyotishpura, capital of the Kamarupa kingdom.
Q404116: City in central Henan, nicknamed 'Eagle City'.
A major coal-mining and power centre.
Site of the Spring Temple Buddha, one of the tallest statues in the world (128 m with pedestal).
Q204271: Capital of the state of San Luis Potosí, in central Mexico's highlands.
Founded in 1592 after silver was discovered; named after Potosí in Bolivia, a byword for silver wealth.
Its colonial centre has many plazas and baroque churches.
Q1643: City in Metro Manila with Bonifacio Global City, a modern business district on a former army base.
Hosts many embassies and corporate headquarters.
Lies between Laguna de Bay and the Pasig River.
Q486319: Home to many Yi, Miao and other ethnic minorities.
The Baili Azalea forest blooms here in spring; the Zhijin cave is one of China's largest karst caves.
Q274584: Honduras's industrial capital and second city, in the Sula Valley near the Caribbean.
The largest Central American city that is not a capital.
Known for its maquila garment factories.
Was once called one of the most violent cities in the world.
Q57958: City in Jiangsu on the Yangtze where it meets the Grand Canal.
Famous for Zhenjiang black vinegar (Chinkiang vinegar).
Jinshan Temple is linked to the legend of the White Snake.
Was a treaty port and the provincial capital; Pearl S. Buck grew up here.
Q1761: Capital of Ireland, at the mouth of the River Liffey on Dublin Bay.
Founded as a Viking settlement in the 9th century; its name means 'black pool'.
Trinity College has the Book of Kells; the city is the home of Guinness.
City of writers: James Joyce, Oscar Wilde, Samuel Beckett and Bram Stoker were born here.
Q1707092: Twin cities in northern Karnataka; Hubli is the commercial centre, Dharwad the seat of administration and education.
Hubli station has the world's longest railway platform (about 1.5 km).
Dharwad is famous for Hindustani classical music and its milk sweet, Dharwad pedha.
Q1580709: Large township on the East Rand of Gauteng, north of Kempton Park.
Established in 1957 under apartheid, when Black residents were moved from Alexandra and other areas.
Part of the Ekurhuleni metropolitan municipality.
Q29015: City in Sichuan famous for salt: brine wells have been drilled here for about 2,000 years.
The Shenhai Well (1835) was the first well in the world drilled deeper than 1,000 m.
Known for its Lantern Festival, its dinosaur museum and spicy food.
Q3579: Capital of Libya, on the Mediterranean coast.
Founded by the Phoenicians as Oea in the 7th century BC.
The Red Castle (Assaraya al-Hamra) and the Arch of Marcus Aurelius are landmarks.
Ruled by Ottomans and Italians; the US fought the Barbary corsairs here (the 'shores of Tripoli').
Q59209: City in southwestern Guangdong on the South China Sea.
China's 'knife capital': it makes a large share of the country's knives and scissors.
The Nanhai I, a Song-dynasty shipwreck with its cargo, is shown in a museum on Hailing Island.
Q184409: City in São Paulo's metro area, the most populous Brazilian city that is not a state capital.
Home of São Paulo–Guarulhos International Airport, Brazil's busiest airport.
A large industrial and logistics centre.
Q360268: Grew around coal mines since the 1950s.
Known for Kouzi liquor (baijiu) and as an ancient town of the Sui–Tang Grand Canal.
Q29109964: A 'new area' in Hebei about 100 km south of Beijing, launched in 2017 by Xi Jinping.
Being built as a planned city for government offices, companies and universities moved out of Beijing.
Includes Baiyangdian, the largest freshwater lake in northern China.
Planned to reach 5 million people by mid-century.
Q472: Capital of Bulgaria, at the foot of Vitosha mountain.
Called Serdica by the Romans; Constantine the Great is said to have called it 'my Rome'.
The Alexander Nevsky Cathedral is one of the largest Orthodox cathedrals in the world.
Has many mineral springs; its motto is 'Ever growing, never ageing'.
Q1342853: County-level city in Jiangsu under Xuzhou.
Famous for its long avenues of ginkgo trees and ginkgo nuts.
An ancient town of the Pi state, with Han-dynasty tombs.
Q587085: Capital of Kwara State, a Yoruba city in Nigeria's north-central zone.
Seat of a Fulani-led emirate since the 19th century.
Famous for its traditional pottery and the 'aso-oke' woven cloth.
Home of the University of Ilorin.
Q4709: Capital of Lara state; Venezuela's fourth city.
Called the 'Music City of Venezuela'; birthplace of conductor Gustavo Dudamel.
Home of the Divina Pastora procession, one of the largest Marian processions in the world.
Q10393: City in West Java, 50 km south of Jakarta, at the foot of Mount Salak.
Its Botanical Gardens, founded in 1817, are among the oldest in Asia.
Was Buitenzorg, the summer seat of the Dutch governor-general; the Bogor Palace is a presidential palace.
Nicknamed the 'Rain City' for its frequent rain.
Q122044: Capital of Huíla Province and Angola's second city, in the southern highlands.
Founded by settlers from Madeira in the 1880s; called Sá da Bandeira under Portuguese rule.
A Christ the King statue overlooks the city, similar to Rio's.
Near the dramatic Tundavala gap and the Serra da Leba road.
Q404599: City in central Henan at the meeting of the Sha and Li rivers.
China's 'food city': home of Shuanghui (WH Group), the world's largest pork producer.
Site of the Jiahu culture, where some of the oldest playable flutes (bone flutes, about 9,000 years old) were found.
Q242895: Deoband, home of the influential Darul Uloom Islamic seminary, is in the district.
Q215755: City in Hunan on the Xiang River, part of the Changsha–Zhuzhou–Xiangtan cluster.
Mao Zedong was born in Shaoshan, in the prefecture; his childhood home is a pilgrimage site.
Also the hometown of Peng Dehuai, the painter Qi Baishi and tennis player Peng Shuai.
Famous for lotus seeds and betel nut.
Q168193: Holy city of Shia Islam, about 160 km south of Baghdad.
Burial place of Ali, cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet; his shrine has a golden dome.
Wadi-us-Salaam is the largest cemetery in the world.
Its Hawza is a leading Shia seminary; home of Grand Ayatollah Sistani.
Q333928: Capital of Aragua state in north-central Venezuela.
Called the 'Garden City'; the dictator Juan Vicente Gómez made it his base and built much of it.
A centre of the Venezuelan air force and aviation.
Q404529: Capital of the Cao Wei state's founder Cao Cao, who moved the Han emperor here in 196.
The world's biggest centre for making wigs and hair extensions from human hair.
Known for Jun porcelain from Yuzhou.
Q178945: City in northeastern Sichuan; the name means 'centre of Ba'.
A Red Army base area in the 1930s.
Known for the Guangwu Mountain red leaves in autumn and Buddhist cliff carvings.
Q373687: City in northern Shandong on the Yellow River near its delta.
Hometown of Sun Tzu, author of 'The Art of War' (Huimin county).
A big textile and aluminium producer.
Q28996: Port city in western Liaoning on the Liaoxi Corridor between North China and Manchuria.
The 1948 Liaoshen Campaign of the Chinese Civil War was decided here.
Its port is China's northernmost seaport.
Q45313: Afghanistan's third city, in the west near Iran, in the fertile Hari River valley.
A great centre of Persian culture under the Timurids in the 15th century.
The Friday Mosque and the minarets of the Musalla complex are famous; its Citadel dates back to Alexander the Great.
A gateway for trade with Iran and Turkmenistan.
Q165204: Capital of Yucatán, Mexico, near the Gulf coast.
Founded in 1542 on the Maya city of T'ho; its cathedral is the oldest on the American mainland.
Called the 'White City' for its limestone buildings; one of Mexico's safest cities.
Gateway to Chichén Itzá, Uxmal and the cenotes.
Q75091: Steel and coal city in Liaoning, southeast of Shenyang.
Founded as a metallurgical centre in 1915; Benxi Steel was once China's fourth-largest steelmaker.
The 1942 Honkeiko colliery disaster here was the worst coal-mine accident in history.
Known for the Benxi Water Cave, a long underground river.
Q44237: Capital of Mendoza Province in Argentina, at the foot of the Andes.
Argentina's wine capital, famous for Malbec; hosts a big grape harvest festival.
San Martín prepared his army here to cross the Andes and liberate Chile and Peru (1817).
Gateway to Aconcagua, the highest mountain outside Asia.
Q185458: Capital of Balochistan, Pakistan, in a mountain valley at about 1,680 m.
Called the 'Fruit Garden of Pakistan' for its apples, grapes and dried fruits.
Largely destroyed by the 1935 Quetta earthquake.
A trade hub on the road to Kandahar; home of a famous army staff college.
Q515712: City in northern Shaanxi on the edge of the Mu Us Desert and the Loess Plateau.
A former Great Wall garrison town; the Zhenbeitai fortress is one of the Great Wall's largest.
Rich in coal, oil and gas, making it one of China's energy bases.
Q199723: Capital of the Karasi beylik in the 14th century.
The surrounding province has olive groves and the Kazdağları (Mount Ida) mountains.
Q891: City at the confluence of the Volga and Oka rivers; called Gorky from 1932 to 1990.
Founded in 1221; its Kremlin overlooks the rivers.
A big industrial centre (GAZ cars); was closed to foreigners in Soviet times — Andrei Sakharov was exiled here.
Birthplace of writer Maxim Gorky; hosted 2018 World Cup matches.
Q906: Industrial city on the eastern side of the southern Urals.
Called 'Tankograd' in WWII for its tank factories.
A meteor exploded over the city in February 2013, injuring about 1,500 people.
The ancient Bronze Age settlement Arkaim is in the region.
Q52028: The largest city in northern Thailand, in the mountains about 700 km north of Bangkok.
Founded in 1296 as capital of the Lanna kingdom; its old city is a square with a moat.
Has over 300 temples, including Wat Phra That Doi Suthep on the mountain above.
Famous for the Yi Peng lantern festival and elephant sanctuaries.
Q223761: Burkina Faso's second city, in the southwest.
Its Grand Mosque (1880s) is a famous example of Sudano-Sahelian mud architecture.
A centre of music and culture, home to many griots and balafon players.
Q466221: City in northeastern Bangladesh on the Surma River.
The shrine of the Sufi saint Shah Jalal draws many pilgrims.
Many British Bangladeshis have roots here.
Q1557962: Town in Bhadohi district, Uttar Pradesh.
Bhadohi is India's 'carpet city': a major centre of hand-knotted carpet weaving.
Q426868: City in Sichuan where the Dadu, Min and Qingyi rivers meet.
The Leshan Giant Buddha (71 m, carved in a cliff in the 8th century) is the largest stone Buddha in the world.
Mount Emei, one of the Four Sacred Buddhist Mountains, is nearby; both are a World Heritage Site.
Q727: Capital of the Netherlands; the seat of government is The Hague.
Grew from a dam on the Amstel river into the world's leading trade port in the 17th-century Golden Age.
Its ring of canals (Grachtengordel) is a World Heritage Site.
Home of the Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum and the Anne Frank House; more bicycles than people.
Q427097: City in Sichuan southwest of Chengdu.
Hometown of Su Shi (Su Dongpo), the great Song-dynasty poet, and his father and brother.
The Sansu Shrine honours the three Su writers.
Q699777: County-level city under Wenzhou, on Yueqing Bay in Zhejiang.
China's capital of low-voltage electrical products (e.g. Chint and Delixi in Liushi).
Much of the scenic Yandang Mountains lie in its area.
